To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the biophysical and chemical properties of PEI are important for siRNA transfection efficiency.

PEI-mediated siRNA transfection in vitro was dependent on biophysical and structural properties, and that PEI:siRNACs with the appropriate N:P ratios and molecular weight were stable and functional in vitro.

the ability of PEI (polyethylenimines) to transfer functionally siRNA (small interfering RNA) to cells in culture was surprisingly dependent on its molecular weight and structure when compared to its ease of use for plasmid delivery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of polyethyleniminemediated siRNA delivery in vitro.
the biophysical and molecular characteristics of polyethyleneimine (PEi) that are important for the successful delivery of siRNA.
the development and characterization of polymeric gene delivery systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there is a very narrow range of N:P ratio and siRNA concentrations that result in effective siRNA delivery, but that the biophysical characteristics of the nanocomplexes (size, zeta potential and stability) are important determinants in the ability to transfer siRNA to cells.
the 25,00 branched PEI was most successful for siRNA delivery to the HR5-CL 11 cell line in this study.
the biophysical characteristics of PEI:RNA nanocomplexes are important, but not necessarily the only factor that determines their efficacy in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biophysical and/or structural characteristics of the PEI are not the only factors that determine siRNA delivery efficiency.
PEI is a very effective siRNA carrier, but only under very specific conditions.
the PEI 25k is a good choice for siRNA delivery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biophysical characteristics of PEI:RNA complexes are not necessarily predictive of the in vivo performance.
the N:P ratio is the most important parameter to control for successful siRNA delivery.
the N:P ratio, molecular weight, and structure of PEI, as well as the siRNA concentration, must be carefully optimized for successful siRNA delivery in vitro.
